UNTRUSTED SOURCE: not attacker-supplied data but attacker-influenced concurrency triggers — any packet/event that executes the device's softirq-context callback (ndo_start_xmit under NET_TX softirq, timer-driven xmit) while a process-context path (workqueue worker, ioctl, open/firmware/SME request) holds the same lock on that CPU; local or remote traffic and timer expiry are enough to align both sides. UNSAFE USE: process call chain (worker -> driver helper -> hw_tx/enqueue) holds the plain-acquired lock, then a softirq on the same CPU spins forever trying to take that same lock while the holder can never resume — a self-deadlock. CONSEQUENCE: softirq/soft-lockup on one CPU, RCU stall and watchdog splats, device TX stall, repeatable denial of service. The invariant generalizes one level up: a lock shared with a hardirq handler needs irqsave/irq-disable at non-irq sites. Seed (staging ks7010 tx_dev_lock, workqueue xmit path vs xmit callback) is a demonstration only and must never be reported.
